name: David
bio: General remodeling contractor and carpenter, balancing the unpredictable billing cycles of construction projects, tool investments, physical body wear-and-tear, and building a multi-crew business.

stages.stageTitle: The Work Van Transmission & Client Float

selectionSnippet.firstTime: Hey. David here. I do residential kitchens and baths. A client is withholding a $12,000 final milestone check over a paint dispute, and this morning the transmission dropped right out of my Ford work van on the highway ($2,800 estimate). I have material lumber bills due Friday and only $400 in checking.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: David here! You pulled me out of the fire when my work van died years ago. I've expanded to a 3-man crew and need your sharp eye on our cash flow.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: David again. I stopped by when my work van transmission blew out. I had to scrape through with expensive credit card advances back then, but I really need an advisor now.

dialogue.greeting: In the trades, everybody thinks contractors are getting rich. They don't see the weeks where you front $15,000 in tile and cabinets on credit cards while homeowners take two months to release checks.
dialogue.planApproved: That's real peace of mind. Getting that transmission paid off and setting up an escrow account for client materials means I won't lose sleep over supply house bills.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our supply house credit line isn't covered here. If 84 Lumber cuts off my commercial credit, my crew can't work on Monday.

lifeEvent.title: Commercial Van Transmission Blowout
lifeEvent.description: David's primary work truck suffered complete transmission failure, requiring an immediate $2,800 repair bill.

stages.stageTitle: Herniated Disc & The Disability Reality Check

selectionSnippet.firstTime: David here. I'm 38. Last month while hoisting a cast-iron clawfoot tub upstairs, my L4-L5 disc herniated. I couldn't walk for three weeks. I realized with terrifying clarity that if my body gives out, our family has zero income. I need to transition off manual labor into management and secure own-occupation disability insurance.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: David! That materials escrow you set up saved my business when a client withheld payments. But a serious back injury just benched me for a month. It was a wake-up call. I need your guidance to buy proper disability coverage and step off the tools.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: David here again. Missed connecting with you previously. A bad back injury showed me how vulnerable a contractor's income is without proper safety nets. Need your help restructuring.

dialogue.greeting: Lying on an MRI table staring at the ceiling, wondering how my family eats if I can't lift sheetrock anymore... that will humble any tough guy. I have to start thinking like a business owner, not just a set of hands.
dialogue.planApproved: This is huge for my family. The disability insurance policy is active, our emergency reserve is insulated, and we have a path to hire a lead carpenter so I can focus on estimating.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our disability insurance policy wasn't funded in the plan! If my back gives out again, we have zero safety net.

lifeEvent.title: Severe Workplace Back Injury
lifeEvent.description: David suffered a herniated disc on a remodel job site, exposing an urgent need for disability insurance protection.

stages.stageTitle: Stepping Off The Tools & General Contracting Firm

selectionSnippet.firstTime: David here at 44. I successfully stepped off the tools and run Kim Construction Group with two full-time crew leads and 6 subcontractors. I'm bidding on commercial tenant-improvement projects. I need help establishing a formal SEP-IRA and managing escrow retainage.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: David! That disability policy and emergency buffer you designed literally saved our family when I transitioned away from manual labor. Today, Kim Construction runs multiple simultaneous residential and commercial jobs! I want to set up an aggressive retirement plan for my wife and me.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: David here. Over the years I grew my crew into an established contracting firm. I want a trusted advisor to help manage our high-volume seasonal cash flows and retirement.

dialogue.greeting: Showing up to a job site wearing clean boots and a clipboard instead of a 30-pound tool belt felt strange at first. But my crew respects the leadership, and my back hasn't flared up in two years.
dialogue.planApproved: This blueprint is rock-solid. Commercial liability is tied down, retainage escrow is protected, and our SEP-IRA is capturing real retirement wealth for the first time in my life.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our commercial umbrella insurance premium was omitted. With 8 guys on scaffolding, a liability lapse would bankrupt the company.

lifeEvent.title: Commercial General Contracting Scale
lifeEvent.description: David scaled Kim Construction into larger commercial projects, bringing higher revenues and larger escrow requirements.

selectionSnippet.firstTime: David here at 52. My longtime foreman is buying out my 60% stake in Kim Construction over a 5-year seller financing note. I'm transitioning out of daily operations, and I need a conservative capital preservation strategy for my retirement portfolio.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: David! From a broken-down work van at 33 to structuring the succession buyout of Kim Construction to my foreman today—you helped me build a lasting business that supported dozens of families. Now I need your wisdom to prepare for retirement.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: David here. I've reached the point where I'm stepping down from contracting and selling the firm. Looking for your expertise on post-business retirement structuring.

dialogue.greeting: Handing the keys to the company truck and the master shop over to my foreman, who started as an apprentice 12 years ago... I couldn't hold back the tears. We built something honest with our hands.
dialogue.planApproved: This is the retirement freedom I worked 30 years with a hammer to earn. Debt is zero, our portfolio yields steady cash flow, and our home is safe.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our taxable brokerage and low-risk yields aren't allocated properly to outpace inflation in retirement.

lifeEvent.title: Business Succession Seller Buyout
lifeEvent.description: David finalized a structured succession buyout note, receiving monthly principal and interest payouts as he transitions into retirement.
